issues.detail: The Greek 'μη παρων' (not present) is translated as 'khi có mặt' (when present). The Greek implies 'not being present' or 'not in the presence of', whereas the Vietnamese suggests a condition of being present.
The Greek 'πεποιθησει' (confidence/assurance) is rendered as 'lòng tin cậy nghịch' (hostile confidence/trust). The word 'nghịch' (hostile/rebellious) is not in the Greek text.
